title: Grateful Dead Live at Greek Theatre, U. Of California on 1982-05-21
lineage: Sbd Mcassette > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Stellar soundboard capture of a high‑energy ’82 Greek run with smoking Bertha>Greatest and an unforgettable Playin’ > Uncle John’s jam.
ai_review.review: The recording is a crystal‑clear soundboard source that many fans call “stellar” or “insane clarity,” making every nuance of the band audible. Musically the show shines – Bertha into The Greatest, a tight Playin' > Uncle John’s sequence, soaring Bird Song and an exuberant second set, though a few note a minor slip on Black Peter and slightly lower energy than the following night.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews are 4‑5 stars, praising both performance and sound quality; only a single low or mixed comment appears, yielding a strong positive consensus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Multiple reviewers describe the audio as crisp, clear and “stellar,” with no significant drop‑outs or balance issues mentioned.

standout_songs: Bertha > The Greatest Story Ever Told
Playin' in the Band > Uncle John's Jam
show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong transitions, especially the seamless Playin'>UJB segue; second set builds nicely with tight drums, space and a soulful jam ending. A few listeners felt the first night lacked the punch of the following night, but overall flow is praised.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for “higher mobility” on Bird Song, crisp leads on Sugar Magnolia, soaring jams on Big River and a powerful solo during Uncle John’s; generally described as “exactly perfect.”
band_member_comments.Phil: "PHILNESS!!" – noted for strong bass presence, a duel with Jerry in the early part of the second set, and overall powerful low‑end work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent (organ) highlighted as very active throughout Playin' and adding texture; keyboards described as “quite active” and “lovely.”
band_member_comments.Drums: Tight timing noted in the first set, energetic percussion during drums/space, Mikey’s on‑stage drumming antics add excitement.
